title: Partial _safePay shortfall in claim()/stake()/unstake() silently discards user rewards by resetting rewardDebt to the full accrued amount
severityAuditNote: Demoted from High to Medium on second-opinion review. Under the in-scope code the invariant balance >= rewardBudget >= sum(pending) holds (because _updatePool clamps `reward > rewardBudget` and rewardBudget only increases via inflows already settled into balance), so the _safePay capping branch is not naturally reachable for non-dust amounts. The bug is real and the fix is correct, but the live exploit requires an auxiliary invariant break (out-of-scope token drift, future admin withdrawal, or an unrelated bug). Severity therefore meets Medium ('value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements') rather than High ('assets stolen/lost without hypotheticals'). Also note the inconsistent rewardDebt update path in claim() vs stake/unstake which is a code-quality bug worth fixing alongside.
description:
Every payout path computes `pending = (user.amount * accRewardPerShare) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt`, then calls `_safePay(pending)` which caps the transfer at the contract's on-chain `rewardToken` balance. Immediately afterwards, `user.rewardDebt` is unconditionally reassigned to `(user.amount * accRewardPerShare) / ACC_PRECISION` — the FULL accrued amount — regardless of how much was actually paid. If `_safePay` capped the payout (because balance < pending), the difference (`pending - paid`) is permanently lost to the user: their debt jumps to the full accrual as if they had been paid in full.

While the NatSpec on `_safePay` suggests this only covers a 1-wei floor-division drift, the cap in `_safePay` applies to the entire on-chain balance — including situations where the hook reverts future pulls, where the contract's `rewardToken.balanceOf(address(this))` is temporarily low because a prior user's pending was paid, or where admin extraction / bugs have drained the reward token. Any such shortfall silently evaporates from the victim's entitlement.

Additionally, in `claim()` the `user.rewardDebt` is only updated inside the `if (pending > 0)` branch, while in `stake()`/`unstake()` it is always updated — inconsistent control flow that should be reconciled.
impact: Users who hit a balance-capped claim lose any unpaid portion permanently. The lost reward does not remain claimable next interaction because `rewardDebt` has advanced to the full accrued share. This also violates the stated invariant `balance == rewardBudget + totalDebt` in the user's favor/protocol's disfavor in the direction of silently-zeroed user debt.
proof: Sequence: (1) user A has accrued 100 phUSD of entitlement; (2) contract balance briefly drops to 60 phUSD (e.g., another user claimed, transient ordering); (3) A calls claim(); `pending = 100`, `_safePay` returns 60; (4) `user.rewardDebt` is bumped to the full `(amt*acc)/PREC`, erasing the 40 phUSD gap. No subsequent claim will recover the 40 phUSD.
recommendation: After `_safePay`, only advance `rewardDebt` by the paid amount, not the full accrual. Minimal masterchef-preserving fix: compute `unpaid = pending - paid`, then set `user.rewardDebt = (user.amount * accRewardPerShare) / ACC_PRECISION - unpaid;` so the unpaid portion rolls into next-call pending. Equivalently: `user.rewardDebt += paid;` (being careful to keep the arithmetic consistent with any later stake/unstake that rewrites rewardDebt from scratch). Alternatively, revert when `_safePay` cannot pay in full and rely on `emergencyWithdraw` as the escape hatch — but only if the protocol can guarantee `balance >= pending` always (not true today given pull() timing). Also reconcile `claim()` to unconditionally update `user.rewardDebt` (matching stake/unstake) and add unit tests that simulate a partial-payout scenario.
mergeNote: ES-03 merged in: same root cause. ES-03 framed this as a latent self-griefing path — any ordinary ordering of user actions where balance is momentarily short (e.g. another user front-runs and drains via legitimate claim, or dispatcher pull hasn't caught up) triggers the silent forfeiture. The per-occurrence loss equals the balance shortfall at claim time, which can be arbitrary (not bounded to 1-wei dust as the _safePay NatSpec implies).
